en: The Characteristics of Images as Spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Homage to the Buddha! (p. 126)
Thus have I heard: at one time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Jeta’s Grove.
At the time when he was about to depart from the sublime Tuṣita palace to go to his mother to teach the Dharma, Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, once the Blessed One has departed or passed into parinirvāṇa, how should faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family conduct themselves?"

The Blessed One said: "Śāriputra, when I have departed or entered final nirvāṇa, my body should be made as symmetrical as a nyagrodha tree. To the extent that the body is, so should the fathom-length be; to the extent that the fathom-length is, so should the body be. An image should be fashioned for the purpose of worship and honor."

The state of robustness, beauty, grace, and elegance residing in all the primary and secondary limbs and members [is attained] due to the excellent configuration of the head, which is shaped like an umbrella, and because the *uṣṇīṣa* is well-situated upon the shoulders;
therein [reside] its length, breadth, and height.
I shall explain the measurements of the Bodhisattvas and the Sugatas according to their proportions and the emergence of their joints; listen to that.
In that regard, first, the measurement of the Bodhisattvas is one hundred and twenty [finger-breadths] by their own finger-measure, and that of the Buddhas is one hundred and twenty-five.
The uṣṇīṣa and the location of the hair are each four finger-breadths; likewise, the portion for the face consists of three and a half times thirteen units. // 1 //
The forehead and the nose, extending downward to the chin, constitute the third [measurement].
The forehead should be four finger-breadths wide and equal in measure to the nose. // 2 //

The chin should extend slightly beyond the end [of the face], and the chin itself should be two finger-breadths [in thickness]; its length and its projection are both desired to be four finger-breadths. // 3 //
The two cheeks, four finger-breadths wide, extend out from the roots of the ears;
the jaw should be three finger-breadths in height and two finger-breadths in width.
That [upper lip] should be more prominent and full, like the jaw of a great lion;
the lower lip should be two finger-breadths in length and one finger-breadth in thickness.
In the middle, there should be a beautiful line; the two corners of the mouth are known as the *mātṛkā*s. A wise person should fashion the face with a length of four finger-breadths.
The forty teeth are said to be situated as they naturally arise;
the upper lip shall be half a finger [in width], and its thickness and protrusion shall be the same. // 7 //
The nose should be made three parts of a finger-breadth, and its base (godhi) is situated right there;
it is two fingers broad and one and a half fingers high.
The two nostrils of the nose are known to be equal, each measuring half a finger-breadth in circumference;
the bridge of the nose is even in the middle, with a width of half a mātrā.
The space between the eyes should be known as one finger-breadth (aṅgula), and each eye is four fingers-breadths [in length].
They are two fingers-breadths in width at the middle, and the pupil of each is one-third of that.
The pupil should be one-fifth [of the eye's width], measuring two or three finger-breadths for those two;
the iris should extend by a fourth part of a finger-breadth, and the eye-socket should be well-rounded.
The socket of the eye should be made in the shape of a lotus petal, measuring three finger-breadths;
the thread for the two eyes should be equal to a *karavīra* flower, [extending] to the nostrils.
One should join the corners of the mouth at the level of the ears;
the space between the eyebrows should be made one and a half finger-breadths wide. (13)
In the center, the ūrṇā should be known as auspicious, resembling the full moon;
likewise, the ūrṇā on the crown of the head is like the bridge of the nose.
Established in glory. // 14 //
He should be known as Śiromaṇi, Suprabha, and likewise Vimala;
the head above the forehead measures four finger-breadths in height.
The [forehead] is shaped like an umbrella, auspiciously blue, with a clockwise curl rising upward;
the brow-line should be four *mātrās* wide, and the tip of the ear should be equal to that. (16)
The two ears protrude by two finger-breadths; their width is known to be half a mātrā, their height one mātrā, and they are joined at the ear-lobes by half a mātrā. // 17 //
The ear-whorl (karṇāvarta), however, is a fourth part of a finger in width;
it should be one and a half fingers [in height], while the space between the ears is two fingers. // 18 //
The two sides should be made as beautiful as possible, and the hair likewise;
the ear-ornament should extend from the outer corner of the eye to a measure of four and a half units.
The head, extending from one ear-tip to the other, is eighteen finger-breadths (aṅgulas) long;
the back is fourteen finger-breadths, and the distance between these two is desired [to be the same]. (20)
The head should be forty mātras in circumference;
from the base of the neck, its height is four mātras and its width is eight mātras.
The circumference should be made twenty-four finger-breadths;
from the neck downwards there are eight finger-breadths,
and the shoulders are twelve finger-breadths.
The space between the shoulders should be rounded, and the shoulder itself should possess the auspicious marks;
the length of the arm is desired to be exactly forty finger-breadths.
The upper arm (bāhu) is twenty units in measure, and the forearm (prabāhu) is likewise sixteen;
the hand (hasta), from the wrist (maṇibandha) to the tips of the fingers, is proclaimed to be twelve aṅgulas. // 24 //
From the wrist to the base of the fingers, it is recorded as one finger-breadth for each finger;
the circumference of the middle of the arm is desired to be twenty *mātṛkā*s.
The forearm should be sixteen [units] long, and the wrist-joint (maṇibandhana) should be twelve;
the length of the hand should be seven, and the width of the palm five.
The conch and the discus are placed upon the soles, as are the lotus, the vajra, and the goad; they possess the forms of all the [major] marks. Le... (re...)
Various kinds of sacrificial pits (khā) should be constructed. // 27 //
The middle finger should be five finger-breadths in length; the index finger should be half a joint shorter;
and the ring finger should be made half a finger-breadth shorter still. (28)
The little finger should be made one joint shorter than the ring finger;
all fingers should have three joints, and the nails should be auspicious, measuring half a joint.
Above the wrist, that thumb is four finger-breadths long;
its circumference is the same, and its nail is half a joint in length.
The space between the thumb and the forefinger is recorded as three finger-breadths;
the little finger should extend five finger-breadths from the wrist.
The span of the hand from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the middle finger should be known as twelve finger-breadths (aṅgulas);
the inclusion of one's own fingers [for measurement] should be one-third of that length. // 32 //
The distance between the neck and the heart is twelve and a half mātrās;
likewise, the distance between the heart and the navel, as well as between the two breasts, is four [mātrās] each.
Above the two breasts, the armpits should be made six *aṅgulas* wide;
from there upward to the shoulders, it is proclaimed to be nine measures (*mātrā*).
The width of the chest should also be twenty-five units;
the circumference of the chest should be made three times its width for an auspicious result. (35)
The space between the breasts and the navel is desired to be sixteen finger-breadths; the depth from the joints and the apertures to the navel-circle is one finger-breadth.
The circumference from the center of the navel is forty-six finger-breadths,
and the waist should be eighteen finger-breadths in width.
The distance between the navel and the penis should be twelve and a half finger-breadths (*mātrikā*); the circumference of the penis at the base of the anus should be half of that. (38)
The two testicles are five finger-breadths in length and four finger-breadths in width; their breadth and length are both five finger-breadths each. (39)
The two thighs should be made symmetrical and twenty-five *mātrikās* in length;
the distance between them at their widest part should be measured as twelve finger-breadths.
The auspicious circumference should also be made thirty-six finger-breadths;
in the middle, from the knees downward, it should be four finger-breadths. // 41 //

The joints and ligaments are firm with a duration of four mātrās; the knees and ankles are well-formed with three and two [mātrās] respectively; the ankles are hidden, the veins and bones are well-set, and the feet are delicate, beautiful, and auspicious.
The shanks are straight and twenty-five *mātrikās* in length;
the circumference between them is twenty-one *mātrikās*. // 43 //
The length [of the leg] is fourteen finger-breadths down to the ankles; the ankle is four finger-breadths [in height];
the foot is twelve finger-breadths in length and half a foot (six finger-breadths) in width.
The two sides are two finger-breadths in width, and the heels are four finger-breadths;
the width of the [fore]feet is six finger-breadths, and their circumference is three times that. // 45 //
The five fingers have two joints each, and the nails are said to be half a joint in length.
The circumference of the thumb is five finger-breadths, and it is three finger-breadths in length.
The forefinger is equal in length to the thumb; the remaining fingers are each shorter than the preceding one by a sixteenth, an eighth, and an eighth [of a finger-breadth] respectively. (47)
The fingers are one mātrā in height, while the thumb is one and a half mātrās;
there, his copper-colored nails are one and a half finger-breadths long, soft and elongated. // 48 //
His feet are like the back of a tortoise, full and adorned externally; they are even, closely set, arching, without gaps, and well-established with the [auspicious] marks. // 49 //
One should have their soles fashioned with beautiful patterns such as wheels and the like;
the omniscient ones, who have destroyed all defilements, praise this feature of the feet.
The egg of a hen, the shape of a sesame seed, the quadrangular, and the perfectly circular—these are the four types of faces for all common liṅgas. (51)
For great men and goddesses, the form should be like a hen’s egg or a sesame seed;
it should be beautiful and pleasing to behold, and one should fashion it with two faces.
For those who are hungry ghosts (preta), spirits (bhūta), goblins (piśāca), and demons (rakṣas) of deformed appearance,
one should have a square mandala constructed with two openings.
The gaze of the Buddhas, the all-seeing ones, is even and serene when looking; it is neither downward nor upward, nor is it joined with any dejection. (54)
Thus ends the description of the characteristics of images as spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One.
